_comment: Transparent rubric. It is published *before* the run so the scoring is not chosen after seeing which method won. Every row the run produces is graded by these rules and no others.

grades.label: official_primary
grades.definition: A page on the organisation's own official domain, or on the domain of its governing public body, that states the fact directly.
examples: a council page listing its own venue

grades.label: official_secondary
grades.definition: A page on an official domain that corroborates the fact but does not state it directly (for example an annual report, a governance page, a public register).
grades.note: Two B rows for the same fact may be aggregated, but the aggregate is recorded as B, never promoted to A.

grades.label: third_party_authoritative
grades.definition: A recognised public reference (national register, government open-data portal, an established encyclopaedia) that is not the organisation's own domain.
grades.note: May be used to *locate* an official page. Never sufficient on its own to accept a field.

grades.label: aggregator_or_directory
grades.definition: A commercial directory, ticketing site, review site or venue-hire broker.
grades.note: Explicitly excluded by the brief when it is the organisation's only presence in the geography.

grades.label: search_snippet_only
grades.definition: A search-result title/snippet with no retrieved page behind it.
grades.note: Treating a snippet as the source is one of the owner's zero-tolerance items.

grades.label: challenge_or_login_page
grades.definition: A CAPTCHA, 'verify you are human', consent-wall or login page returned in place of the content.
grades.note: Must never be persisted as validated evidence, even when served with HTTP 200.

field_acceptance._comment: A field is accepted only on a grade that counts_as_evidence, and only when the excerpt hash is present.
field_acceptance.rule: accepted(field) := source.grade in {A,B} AND source.url_accessible_at(retrieved_at) AND excerpt_sha256 is a 64-char lowercase hex AND the excerpt actually contains the field value
field_acceptance.otherwise: the row is emitted with verification=PENDING or UNVERIFIED, never as a fact

measurements.definition: accepted rows whose official_domain resolves on the organisation's own site / accepted rows
candidate facts with an accessible source page AND excerpt hash / candidate facts
rows a human reviewer accepted / rows submitted
duplicate candidate rows per accepted entity
required fields absent from accepted rows
accepted rows a reviewer later rejected, per reviewer-checked sample
provider spend in USD / accepted rows
provider credits or units / accepted rows
count by closed-set reason code across all attempts

comparison_rule: Methods are compared on cost per human-accepted valid result, not on API call count. A cheaper method that yields no accepted rows is not cheaper.

blind_audit.definition: The reviewer scores a subset without seeing which method produced which row, and the subset is drawn so it is independently checkable afterwards.
blind_audit.two_pass: pass 1 scores the row; pass 2 re-checks the cited source page still resolves and still contains the excerpt.
